features.text: Patient mentioned that she wishes it were under better circumstances.
Patient confirmed that the biopsy indicated melanoma.
Patient first noticed the spot when her mother noticed it during a visit last month.
Patient visited a dermatologist on April 10th to get the spot checked.
Patient has a family history of melanoma, with her mother and her mother's sister affected.
Patient's grandfather had pancreatic cancer on her mother's side.
Patient has not had any skin spots checked out previously that were cancerous or precancerous.
Patient's primary care doctor has not expressed concern about any of her moles in the past.
Patient owns an auto repair shop.
Patient is a current smoker, having started in her teens.
Patient has had gallbladder and appendix surgery.
Patient has not experienced any significant health issues recently and feels great.
On the right inferior back, there is a one-centimeter shave biopsy site with no residual pigmentation.
No intrinsic or satellite lesions, no other suspicious moles, and no lymphadenopathy were found.
A soft, nontender lymph node was found in the right groin.
Patient expressed concern about the biopsy result but was reassured by the doctor.
Patient acknowledged the importance of applying sunscreen as advised by the dermatologist.
Patient agreed to schedule an ultrasound and has no immediate questions.
